exchanges.title: Copilot asks the MCP server for access
exchanges.summary: Copilot sends its first MCP request without an access token. The server replies with an authentication challenge.

exchanges.title: Copilot discovers who can authorize access
exchanges.summary: The MCP server's metadata identifies the protected resource, its permissions, and the authorization server: Microsoft Entra.

exchanges.title: Copilot tries OAuth metadata
exchanges.summary: MCP mandates an ordered metadata search. Copilot tries the first location; its 404 leads to the second location in exchange 04.

exchanges.title: Copilot tries an OpenID discovery alternative
exchanges.summary: The second location in MCP's required discovery order also returns 404. Copilot then tries the third location in exchange 05.

exchanges.title: Copilot finds Entra's endpoints
exchanges.summary: The third location succeeds. Copilot validates the issuer and uses the authorization and token endpoints in this document; no fourth metadata location is required.

exchanges.title: The browser carries Copilot's authorization request
exchanges.summary: Copilot opens the browser with the authorization URL. Alongside the MCP permission, it requests offline_access so Entra can issue a refresh token for later renewal. Entra's HTTP 200 response includes a script that sends the browser to Copilot with the authorization code; see the Response tab.

exchanges.title: The browser returns an authorization code to Copilot
exchanges.summary: The authorization code is in the browser's GET request query, not this exchange's response. Copilot receives code and state at its local callback and returns HTTP 200 to the browser.

exchanges.title: Copilot exchanges the code for tokens
exchanges.summary: Copilot sends the code and its secret verifier directly to Entra over HTTPS. Entra checks the PKCE proof and other grant conditions before issuing tokens.

exchanges.title: Copilot retries with an access token
exchanges.summary: The server validates Copilot's access token and answers server/discover. capabilities.tools advertises tool support; actual tool definitions arrive with tools/list in exchange 10.

exchanges.title: Copilot discovers the available tools
exchanges.summary: Authorization now accompanies MCP requests. The server returns a tool definition so Copilot knows the tool's name and accepted arguments.

tools.name: get_weather
tools.description: Get the current weather for a city.

jsonrpc.why: Tells the receiver how to interpret the message envelope; it is separate from the MCP revision.

id.why: Lets the client match a result or error to its request, independently of the HTTP connection.
id.values: MCP requests use a string or integer, never null; responses echo that ID. Notifications have no ID. Do not reuse an outstanding request's ID.

method.what: The RPC operation the client is requesting.
method.why: Selects the operation and therefore the schema of params and result.
method.values: A string such as server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, resources/read, or prompts/get; each has its own requirements.

params.why: Carries operation arguments and per-request MCP metadata.
params.values: An object; allowed properties depend on method. Modern requests must carry required _meta values even when the operation has no business arguments.

_meta.what: Protocol and extension metadata attached to an MCP message.
_meta.why: Modern MCP is stateless: each request declares its own version and client capabilities rather than relying on a prior handshake.
_meta.values: An object. Reserved io.modelcontextprotocol/* keys have defined schemas; vendor keys follow the metadata naming rules.

io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolversion.what: The MCP revision used by this request.
io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolversion.why: Allows each request to be interpreted independently and lets the server reject unsupported revisions.
io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolversion.values: A supported date-form version string; here 2026-07-28. Required on modern requests and must match the HTTP MCP-Protocol-Version header.

io.modelcontextprotocol/clientinfo.why: Makes the client identifiable for display and diagnostics without a connection-level initialization step.
io.modelcontextprotocol/clientinfo.values: An Implementation object with name and version, optionally title/icons/websiteUrl. Recommended on each request; not an authenticated identity.

io.modelcontextprotocol/serverinfo.why: Identifies the replying implementation for display and diagnostics.
io.modelcontextprotocol/serverinfo.values: An Implementation object with name/version and optional presentation fields. Recommended in result._meta; not proof of server identity.

io.modelcontextprotocol/clientcapabiliti.what: The client features available to this request.
io.modelcontextprotocol/clientcapabiliti.why: The server must not require a capability the client did not declare.
io.modelcontextprotocol/clientcapabiliti.values: A required ClientCapabilities object, possibly empty. Feature objects can describe roots, sampling, elicitation, subscriptions, or extensions as defined by their schemas.

result.why: Contains the operation's output, such as discovery information or tool definitions.
result.values: An object whose schema depends on method. A response has result or error, not both.

resulttype.what: The kind of successful MCP result.
resulttype.why: Lets the client distinguish a completed operation from one requiring more input.
resulttype.values: "complete" or "input_required"; supported extensions may add types. An absent value is treated as "complete" for older implementations.

supportedversions.why: Allows a client to select a mutually supported revision before invoking other methods.
supportedversions.values: An array of protocol-version strings in the discovery result.

capabilities.what: The features advertised by the server.
capabilities.why: Lets clients learn which kinds of operations are supported.
capabilities.values: An object with supported feature keys such as tools, resources, prompts, logging, and extensions. An empty feature object can still advertise support.

tools.what: Tools the server exposes, or its tool-support capability.
tools.why: The discovery capability advertises support; the tools/list result provides the actual callable definitions.
tools.values: In capabilities: a feature object. In tools/list result: an array, possibly empty, of Tool objects.

tool.what: One Tool definition returned by tools/list.
tool.why: Describes an operation and its accepted inputs before the client invokes it.
tool.values: An object with name and inputSchema; description, title, outputSchema, annotations, and icons provide additional information.

inputschema.what: The JSON Schema for a tool's arguments.
inputschema.why: Tells the client what input shape, field types, and constraints to use in tools/call.
inputschema.values: A valid JSON Schema object, not null. Defaults to JSON Schema 2020-12 unless $schema specifies another supported dialect.

name.what: A machine-readable name in the containing protocol object.
name.why: Identifies an implementation, tool, or requested operation argument, depending on the parent.
name.values: A string. Tool names are case-sensitive and should be 1–128 characters using letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, and dot.

title.why: Provides a readable UI name without changing the machine identifier.
title.values: A string; it does not replace the tool's name for invocation.

description.what: Human-readable documentation supplied by the server.
description.why: Explains a tool's behavior or a parameter's purpose to Copilot and the language model.
description.values: A string. Tool and schema descriptions are application-defined, not standardized MCP vocabulary.

version.why: Provides diagnostic context for the reported client or server.
version.values: A string such as 1.0.0; this is not necessarily the date-form MCP protocol version.

url.what: Support for out-of-band URL-mode user interactions.
url.why: Lets a server direct sensitive interactions to an external site without passing credentials through the MCP client.
url.values: An object, often empty, under elicitation capabilities. A url field in an actual input request is instead a destination string.

ttlms.what: The server's cache lifetime for this result.
ttlms.why: Lets the client avoid fetching unchanged discovery/list data unnecessarily.
ttlms.values: A non-negative integer in milliseconds; 0 means immediately stale. Required for modern complete discovery/list results; absent/negative values are treated as 0.

cachescope.what: The permitted reuse scope of a cached result.
cachescope.why: Distinguishes results reusable across callers from those tied to one authorized caller.
cachescope.values: "public" or "private", interpreted together with ttlMs and the caching rules; not an OAuth scope.

mcp-protocol-version.what: An HTTP mirror of the request's MCP revision.
mcp-protocol-version.why: Allows intermediaries to inspect the requested protocol without parsing JSON.
mcp-protocol-version.values: A date-form version string matching params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion']; required on modern POST requests.

mcp-method.what: An HTTP mirror of the JSON-RPC method.
mcp-method.why: Lets gateways route or inspect requests using headers.
mcp-method.values: The same method string as the body; required for modern MCP requests. A mismatch is a protocol error.

accept.what: Response media types the client can receive.
accept.why: Lets the server choose JSON or streamed SSE for an MCP response.
accept.values: Modern MCP POSTs must list both application/json and text/event-stream.

content-type.what: The media type of this message's body.
content-type.why: Determines how to decode the bytes before interpreting their fields.
content-type.values: MCP requests: application/json. MCP responses: application/json or text/event-stream. OAuth token forms: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

host.what: The destination authority of the HTTP request.
host.why: Identifies the target server separately from the path or OAuth client ID.
host.values: A hostname with an optional port, such as mcp.example.com or 127.0.0.1:49152.

status.why: Reports the HTTP-layer outcome independently of any JSON-RPC result or error.
status.values: An integer: 401 is the auth challenge here, 404 is a failed metadata candidate, and 200 is HTTP success.

authorization.why: Lets the resource server authenticate/authorize the caller using an issued access token.
authorization.values: The "Bearer" scheme followed by the access token Entra issued to Copilot. Copilot does not send this header on its initial unauthenticated request.

www-authenticate.why: Tells the client how to obtain authorization and where to discover resource metadata.
www-authenticate.values: A Bearer challenge with parameters such as resource_metadata, scope, realm, and error; the response is 401 here.

resource_metadata.what: The URL of the protected-resource metadata document.
resource_metadata.why: Provides the discovery starting point after the unauthenticated MCP request.
resource_metadata.values: An absolute metadata URL advertised in WWW-Authenticate; it is not the token endpoint.

client_id.what: The application's identifier at the authorization server.
client_id.why: Identifies the registered OAuth client in the browser authorization request and token exchange.
client_id.values: An opaque application identifier, not necessarily a UUID and not a secret. This example uses a pre-registered public client.

response_type.why: Selects an authorization-code flow rather than asking the browser to receive an access token directly.
response_type.values: For this flow: "code". Other OAuth response types belong to other flows and are not substitutes here.

redirect_uri.what: The destination for the browser's authorization callback.
redirect_uri.why: Returns the code to the local client rather than to the MCP resource server.
redirect_uri.values: A registered callback URI; native apps can use a loopback HTTP listener with an ephemeral port. The token request must use the same redirect URI where required.

scope.what: The permissions requested or granted for access.
scope.why: The MCP API scope grants access to that server. Copilot adds offline_access to ask Entra for a refresh token; it is not another MCP API permission.
scope.values: A space-separated list: the MCP API permission plus offline_access in the authorization request. Offline means the user need not be interacting with the app, not that network access is unnecessary.

state.what: A value Copilot uses to recognize its own browser callback.
state.why: Helps bind the browser callback to the initiating client transaction and mitigate CSRF.
state.values: An opaque value Copilot generates and Entra returns unchanged. Copilot compares it with the value it saved before opening the browser.

code_challenge.what: A hash-based commitment that Copilot sends through the browser to Entra.
code_challenge.why: Copilot computes this value from its secret verifier. The browser carries it to Entra, which binds it to the authorization code for a later check.
code_challenge.values: For S256: unpadded base64url of SHA-256(ASCII(code_verifier)), producing 43 characters.

code_challenge_method.what: The PKCE transformation applied to the verifier.
code_challenge_method.why: Tells the server how to verify the subsequent proof.
code_challenge_method.values: PKCE defines "plain" and "S256". S256 means SHA-256 followed by unpadded base64url; Copilot uses S256 here.

code_verifier.what: A random secret string created and initially kept by Copilot.
code_verifier.why: Copilot keeps this value out of the browser's authorization URL. When Copilot later sends it directly to Entra, Entra hashes it and compares the result with the challenge bound to the code.
code_verifier.values: 43–128 unreserved ASCII characters: letters, digits, hyphen, period, underscore, or tilde. Copilot must generate a fresh, cryptographically random value for each authorization attempt.

code.what: The short-lived authorization code Entra issues after authorization.
code.why: Connects the browser authorization step to the client's back-channel token exchange.
code.values: An opaque, single-use value. It is not an access token and should not be interpreted by the client.

grant_type.what: The token endpoint operation being requested.
grant_type.why: Tells the authorization server which grant-specific validation and fields to apply.
grant_type.values: Here "authorization_code". To renew access using a refresh token, Copilot would make a separate request with "refresh_token".

access_token.what: The credential issued for resource access.
access_token.why: Is presented to the MCP server in the Authorization header.
access_token.values: An opaque credential from Copilot's perspective. The MCP server validates it, including its intended audience and permissions.

refresh_token.what: A credential for obtaining new access tokens.
refresh_token.why: Copilot stores it securely and later sends it only to Entra's token endpoint to obtain a new access token. It is not sent to the MCP server.
refresh_token.values: An opaque secret; optional in the token response. Its presence does not mean a refresh grant was exercised.

token_type.what: How the issued access token is to be used.
token_type.why: Specifies the authorization scheme for subsequent resource requests.
token_type.values: Here "Bearer"; token-type values are case-insensitive. The actual token remains secret.

expires_in.what: The access-token lifetime reported at issuance.
expires_in.why: Helps the client plan renewal before expiry.
expires_in.values: A numeric duration in seconds; this is a response field, not independent evidence of token validity.

resource.why: In metadata it names the API; as an OAuth request parameter it targets the token to that API.
resource.values: An absolute resource URI without a fragment. The metadata field does not substitute for the resource parameter required on modern MCP authorize/token requests.

authorization_servers.what: Authorization servers trusted for this resource.
authorization_servers.why: Tells the MCP client where to discover authorization and token endpoints.
authorization_servers.values: An array of issuer identifiers containing at least one authorization server for MCP.

issuer.why: Binds discovered metadata and authorization responses to the expected server.
issuer.values: An HTTPS issuer URL that must match the identifier used for discovery; it is not client_id or the resource URI.

authorization_endpoint.what: Where the browser requests user authorization.
authorization_endpoint.why: Provides the front-channel endpoint used with client_id, scope, redirect_uri, and PKCE.
authorization_endpoint.values: An HTTPS URL obtained from validated server metadata.

token_endpoint.what: Where the OAuth client exchanges grants for tokens.
token_endpoint.why: Provides the back-channel endpoint used by Copilot, not by the MCP server.
token_endpoint.values: An HTTPS URL; this flow sends a form-encoded POST containing code, verifier, and client ID.

scopes_supported.what: Scopes advertised by this metadata document.
scopes_supported.why: Provides permission-discovery hints; the challenged/requested/granted scope sets are separate.
scopes_supported.values: An array of case-sensitive strings; interpretation depends on whether this is resource or authorization-server metadata.

schema.type.what: The JSON type allowed at this schema location.
schema.type.why: Constrains or documents tool inputs/outputs; actual argument values are defined by the application.
schema.type.values: A type name or array: object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, null.

schema.properties.what: Schemas for named properties of an object.
schema.properties.why: Constrains or documents tool inputs/outputs; actual argument values are defined by the application.
schema.properties.values: A map from application-defined property names to subschemas; names are not MCP standard fields.

schema.required.what: Properties that must be present in an object.
schema.required.why: Constrains or documents tool inputs/outputs; actual argument values are defined by the application.
schema.required.values: An array of property-name strings; other constraints determine valid values.

schema.additionalproperties.what: Whether unspecified object properties are permitted.
schema.additionalproperties.why: Constrains or documents tool inputs/outputs; actual argument values are defined by the application.
schema.additionalproperties.values: A boolean or subschema; false rejects properties not otherwise covered.

tools.capability.what: The server advertises support for tools; this is not a list of tool definitions.
tools.capability.why: server/discover describes features the server implements. Copilot uses tools/list separately to obtain tool names, descriptions, and schemas.
tools.capability.values: A capability object. {} means support with no optional settings; it does not mean the server has zero tools.

tools.list.what: The actual tool definitions returned by tools/list.
tools.list.why: Gives Copilot the names, descriptions, and input schemas of tools available to its authorization context.
tools.list.values: An array of Tool objects, possibly empty. This is distinct from the capabilities.tools object returned by server/discover.
